notes: The point geocodes the street address printed on the Nevis directions page, so it is building-grade at best; the cyclotron hall position is not given by any source consulted.

summary.plain: The Columbia University physics laboratory at Irvington, New York, about 20 miles north of Manhattan, where a cyclotron was built after the Second World War.
summary.technical: Columbia University's Nevis Laboratories, 136 South Broadway, Irvington, New York; site of the Nevis synchrocyclotron used by the 1957 Garwin-Lederman-Weinrich parity experiment.
